alert.summary: CloudWatch alarm fired for ECS service checkout

logs: EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd_warden-pg(<UUID_1>)
EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z_warden-pg(<UUID_2>)
checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd/checkout 2026-09-24T12:52:15.066838486Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising
checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z/checkout 2026-09-24T12:52:08.142306796Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising

root_cause.hypothesis: checkout container OOM-killed due to undersized memory limit (48 MiB) vs actual usage — logs show container allocating ~900MiB cache shortly after start, far exceeding limit, causing OOM kill and CrashLoopBackOff restarts
evidence: log line 'allocating 900MiB cache' directly precedes crash pattern
WARN memory pressure rising in both pods before restart
restart_count=12 consistent with repeated OOM/backoff cycle
BackOff events confirm CrashLoopBackOff-style restart, though crashloop_containers metric reads 0 (likely lag/threshold artifact)
ruled_out: bad deploy — RECENT DEPLOYS empty, no deploy correlation
node-level resource exhaustion — only checkout containers affected, not node-wide signal in evidence

proposal.reasoning: Memory limit set at 48 MiB, but container log shows allocating ~900MiB cache shortly after start. Both pods OOM-killed (oom_killed_containers=2), restart_count=12, CrashLoopBackOff. Root cause is undersized memory limit vs actual workload need, not a bad deploy (recent deploys empty) or transient load spike. Restarting pods alone won't fix it — they'll OOM again immediately.
proposal.expected_effect: Increase task memory limit for checkout (e.g. to >=1024 MiB) so cache allocation fits; pods stop OOM-killing, restart_count stabilizes, pods_ready returns to 2/2.

reasons: Passed all policies. Held for operator approval before execution.
